explanation: Fringes of skin on its long hind toes spread as they slap the water, and each stroke traps a pocket of air. Light youngsters manage it far better than heavy adults.

claims.text: Basilisk lizards can run across the surface of water on their hind legs.
Green iguanas, spiny-tailed iguanas and anoles cannot run across water.
Basilisks have fringes of skin on their hind toes that spread out when they slap the water.
Each footstroke of a running basilisk creates a pocket of air that helps keep it up.
Young, lighter basilisks run on water more easily than heavy adults.
